minutes.headline: Select Board voted 3-2 against directing the town manager to look for a more accessible meeting space.
minutes.summary: The board transferred the Embers Pizzeria liquor licenses, renewed seven earth removal permits over a split on how the motion was framed, and debated moving meetings out of Town Hall for ADA reasons. The state primary warrant was approved and board liaisons were assigned. The town manager reported on DPW staffing shortages and COVID, and the board went into executive session on litigation.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member cited an estimate for the town hall at TCP; another member said no cost estimates have been presented to the design committee.
A member said the fiscal year 22 budget will be abysmal and demand the town manager's attention.
The town manager said the DPW cannot fill three equipment operator vacancies because of the low rate of pay and a lack of qualified candidates.
State travel order failure to comply may bring a fine per day.
A member noted that the earlier 275th committee received some money for parades and fireworks.

decisions.decision: The Proctor permit renewal will carry a stipulation that the rear berm is completed by the end of November, with the building commissioner to follow up.
Fence viewer appointment of the applicant was postponed so the applicant can appear and the board can ask questions.
The June 9 minutes were deferred to the next meeting because they were only just received.
The tri-centennial committee will not be formed now; the board agreed it is too early, to revisit in about five years, and no motion was needed.
Liaisons assigned informally: Mr Jeffries to library and council on aging, Mr Dwyer to planning board, Mr Marino to finance committee, the chair to school committee.
No meeting next week; the next meeting is September 1.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 3-2 against directing the town manager to find a more accessible meeting space for board meetings.
The board approved renewals of seven earth removal permits 4-1, with the rear berm on one permit to be completed by the end of November 2020.
The board voted 5-0 to support transfers of the Embers liquor, common victualler and temporary extension of premises licenses.
The board approved the 2020 state primary warrant 5-0 after correcting the poll hours to 7 am to 8 pm.
The town manager said the DPW cannot fill three equipment operator vacancies because of low pay and a lack of qualified candidates.

why_it_matters: Where the board meets decides how easily residents with mobility needs can attend and speak, and the 3-2 vote leaves that question unsettled.
Unfilled DPW positions and a budget a member described as difficult for FY22 point to pressure on road and public works services and on future tax-supported pay decisions.
watch_next: The next Select Board meeting, September 1, 2020, and the deferred June 9 minutes and postponed fence viewer appointment.
TCP building design committee meetings on Aug 31, Sept 10 and Sept 21, open to public input.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the Embers transfers, the primary warrant, the $500 travel fine and most attendees. They differ on the earth removal vote record, the accessibility motions, the fence viewer reason, the Proctor deadline and the DPW figure, and the official omits the TCP cost, the tri-centennial item and the next meeting date. The key point is that the earth removal vote is only partially printed in the official minutes (four ayes, no result), and the permit-60 berm condition is not recorded there, so the 4-1 tally and the November deadline should be checked against the recording.
